index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents three distinct bundle diagrams arranged horizontally from left to right, each representing a different possibilistic model in the context of quantum information theory: the possibilistic CHSH (left), the PR box (middle), and the PR prism (right). Each diagram is a 3D geometric structure composed of black nodes connected by solid and dashed lines, forming polyhedral shapes with labeled vertices.

[1] Global Layout and Structure:
The overall layout consists of three separate diagrams placed side-by-side on a white background. The leftmost diagram is a complex 3D structure resembling a cube with additional internal connections and an extended lower base. The middle diagram is a simpler cube-like structure with fewer internal edges. The rightmost diagram is a prism-shaped structure with triangular bases and rectangular sides, appearing more compact than the first two. All diagrams share a consistent visual style with black nodes and lines, and labels positioned near or at the nodes.

[2] Visual Modules and Attributes:
Each diagram features black circular nodes connected by black lines. Solid lines represent direct connections between nodes, while dashed vertical lines indicate structural alignment or projection between upper and lower layers. Nodes are labeled with numerical values (0 or 1) or variable names (a₁, a₂, b₁, b₂, x₁, x₂, x₃). In the left diagram, the top layer has four nodes labeled 1, 1, 0, 1, and the bottom layer has four nodes labeled a₁, b₁, b₂, a₂. The middle diagram mirrors this labeling but with fewer internal connections. The right diagram has two triangular layers: the top triangle has nodes labeled 1, 0, 0, and the bottom triangle has nodes labeled x₁, x₂, x₃, with a central node labeled 0 connecting vertically via dashed lines.

[3] Connections and Arrows:
Connections are represented by straight lines between nodes. In the left diagram, numerous solid lines form a dense network within the top cube and connect it to the lower quadrilateral base. Dashed vertical lines link corresponding nodes between the top and bottom layers. The middle diagram shows a sparser set of solid lines forming a cube with fewer diagonals, and similar dashed vertical connections. The right diagram features solid lines forming two triangles (top and bottom) and connecting them via vertical dashed lines from each vertex to a corresponding node in the opposite triangle. There are no arrows; all connections are undirected, indicating relationships or possible transitions rather than directional flow. The diagrams collectively illustrate the structure of possibilistic correlations in different theoretical models, with the PR prism being the most geometrically constrained.
